definition: The physical toll that repeated geneware modifications take on the skeletal system over time, resulting in chronic pain, micro-fractures, or degraded bone density. Also used figuratively to describe any hidden long-term cost of short-term enhancement decisions.
origin: Medical slang originating in Helix Biosystems rejection studies, adopted by street docs in the Shelf
usage: Street-level geneware users, black market surgeons, Tier 1-2 clinics
example: Three splice jobs in two years — she's paying the marrow tax now, walks like her hips are made of chalk.
